R1D-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Hills Creek
R1D-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R1D-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2015 (11 years old), 20 m W: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 14 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Hills Creek 50 m E: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from City of Campbell River, about 139 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.97152, -125.51449, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 8.0 km W, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 673 m, about 227 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 1.0 km SE of the spot at 246 m (50.95863, -125.61603). Water: Hills Creek 70 m NW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-15, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R1D-bear-backcountry-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 1-15: about 117 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

R1D-deer-backcountry-0002.name: 130 m N of Millerd Creek
R1D-deer-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).

evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-1-008 unit 28 (official), 80 m N. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2008 (18 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHvm1): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SW facing slope, 17 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).
